content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show downward momentum.
- Shows persistent lag in reacting to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Tends to overreact to short-term volatility, overshooting downward trends after sharp declines.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts often settle near historical averages too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Underestimates price recovery after sharp drops — fails to capture rebound momentum in the first 5–7 days.
- Overestimates price stability in low-volatility periods — fails to adjust for underlying trend shifts.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history includes recent price consolidation rather than sharp moves.
